sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
hindiTranslation: हे पृथानन्दन  यह ब्राह्मी स्थिति है ।  इसको प्राप्त होकर कभी कोई मोहित नहीं होता ।  इस स्थितिमें यदि अन्तकालमें भी स्थित हो जाय, तो निर्वाण शान्त ब्रह्मकी प्राप्ति हो जाती है ॥
englishTranslation: Arjuna, this is the Brahmic state. Having reached it, one is never deluded. Remaining established in it even at the end of life, one attains freedom in the supreme reality.
essence: Steadiness in the supreme reality ends confusion, even at life’s edge.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: A person who reaches this steady inner state is no longer confused. Even at life’s end, that steadiness leads to freedom in the supreme reality.
simpleInsight: A clear mind can stay steady even at life's end.
detailedMeaning: After Krishna describes the still mind that no longer chases desire, he names the result for Arjuna: this is the Brahmic state. A person established in it is free of confusion, and even death cannot undo it.
modernRelevance: In a hospital corridor, a son waits outside the ICU where his mother lies. Panic keeps rising. Krishna speaks of a steadiness that holds even at the end of life, and that is the ground to stand on.
translationLiteral: एषा (this) / ब्राह्मी (of Brahman) / स्थितिः (state) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / न (not) / एनाम् (this) / प्राप्य (having attained) / विमुह्यति (is deluded) / स्थित्वा (having remained established) / अस्याम् (in this) / अन्तकाले (at the end of life) / अपि (even) / ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम् (freedom in Brahman) / ऋच्छति (attains)
insight: Krishna names the brahmic state: once reached, delusion ends, and even at death it holds.

quoteVariants.text: Reach this steady state. Delusion ends, and freedom in the supreme reality remains.
Even at the end, this steadiness carries you through.
Stay steady; delusion cannot touch you.
